summary: Mark procedural colour data with a colour space, mark non-colour data as none, and upload with needsUpdate without treating those pixels as physical properties.
objective: A canvas colour map tagged sRGB and a roughness canvas tagged NoColorSpace stay visually distinct; omitting needsUpdate leaves the last GPU image.
applies_when: A texture is generated or updated at runtime from a canvas, DataTexture or similar source.
Colour maps and data maps share an authoring path and could be mis-tagged.
intent_signals: paint a flow map at runtime
why is my canvas texture too dark
example_prompts: Generate a pond colour canvas as sRGB and a matching roughness canvas as non-colour data.
Update a procedural label texture each time the caption changes, with needsUpdate.
negative_signals: Leaving colourSpace at the default NoColorSpace on a PNG-like colour canvas.
not_for: Display calibration or ICC workflows beyond Three.js sRGB/Linear-sRGB roles.
Claims that a correct colour space validates a physical BRDF.

principles: The working colour space is Linear-sRGB. Tag colour textures according to their actual encoding: SRGBColorSpace for sRGB colour pixels and LinearSRGBColorSpace for linear colour pixels. Non-colour normal or roughness data generally use NoColorSpace. CanvasTexture or DataTexture storage does not determine which meaning the pixels have.
needsUpdate is the upload contract. CanvasTexture sets it true once at construction; later canvas drawing still needs a fresh flag.
A procedural map is appearance or data. It does not become density, friction or temperature unless a separate model reads it as such and says so.
implementation: Create CanvasTexture or DataTexture, set colorSpace from the pixel encoding and role before first use, and keep colour and non-colour sources distinct.
After drawing, set texture.needsUpdate = true. Do not change width, height, format or type in place; dispose and recreate instead.
Record renderer outputColorSpace with the test. Dispose textures when replacing a surface.
Never copy a colour canvas into a roughness slot without retagging NoColorSpace.
observable_checks: A mid-grey sRGB colour canvas and the same bytes tagged NoColorSpace do not match under the same lighting.
Redrawing the canvas without needsUpdate leaves the previous GPU image; setting the flag shows the new drawing.
Changing a roughness canvas does not alter collider friction or mass.

creative_affordances: Hand-painted, noise or data-driven canvases are interchangeable if colour-space tags stay honest.
A split view of colour versus data tagging is a useful teaching layout.
known_limits: Three.js documents sRGB and Linear-sRGB roles for typical web output; wider display gamuts are noted as not the web default.
Authored reusable guidance; no runtime artifact has been observed for this record.

claims.statement: Colour PNG or JPEG textures must be annotated SRGBColorSpace while non-colour textures such as roughness or normal maps use NoColorSpace; Texture.needsUpdate triggers a GPU upload; CanvasTexture sets needsUpdate true at construction because a canvas can be used for rendering immediately.
claims.scope: Three.js colour-management roles and texture upload flags; not a measured BRDF or friction model.

source_refs.locator: Input color space: colour textures SRGBColorSpace, non-colour textures NoColorSpace
colorSpace default NoColorSpace; needsUpdate GPU upload; dimensions/format/type cannot change after first use
